_comment: Plain-language help shown by the small ? next to settings and editor fields. Keys: <screen>.<label slug> (see js/screens/shared/help.js).
setup.name: What students and the debrief call this sim, e.g. "Tuesday med-surg lab".
setup.shift-start: The clock time the sim starts at. Event times are shown on this shift clock.
setup.shift-end-sim-stops-blank-no-end: The sim stops on its own at this time and every clock shows the time left. Leave blank to run until you press End.
setup.speed: How fast sim time runs. 1x is real time; 8x runs an 8-hour shift in an hour. You can change it while running.
setup.assignment: Random: students fill open group slots in the order they join. Manual: only names you list can join, into the group you put them in.
setup.handoff: Once: the report pops up the first time a student opens a patient, then is gone (notes stay). Always: a Handoff tab stays in the chart. Never: no report.
setup.charge-nurse: Who runs the Charge tab (admissions board, unit overview): you, a student, or nobody. With nobody, admissions go straight to their group.
setup.prn-pre-check-window-min: How recent a required check (e.g. a BP before nitro) must be when the order itself doesn't say.
setup.student-priority-scale: The scale students use to prioritize their patients (from priority-scales.json). Your own triage tags stay hidden from them.
setup.students: How many students share this group's patients.
setup.patients: Pick patients yourself, or let the randomizer pick by triage tag counts (never reusing a patient across groups).
setup.student-names-one-per-line: For manual assignment: only these names can join this group.
editor.name: Patient's name as students see it.
editor.sex: As written in your case (e.g. M, F).
editor.room: Room number shown on the unit.
editor.triage-tag-yours: Your answer key. Students never see it; they set their own priority and the debrief compares.
editor.priority-label: Your short note on priority, e.g. "High priority – immediate assessment". Instructor-only.
editor.code-status: e.g. Full code, DNR. Shown on the chart banner.
editor.review-status: Proposed = drafted, not yet checked by you. Mark Approved once you have reviewed it.
editor.source: Where this case came from (for your records).
editor.allergies: One per line as "agent | reaction". Medications given that match are flagged.
editor.allergy-note: Free text when there are no listed allergies, e.g. "No known drug allergies".
editor.hpi: History of present illness, as in your write-up.
editor.pmh: Past medical history, one item per line.
editor.home-meds: One per line as "name | dose | frequency".
editor.shown-when-the-student-assesses-o: Baseline findings. Students only see them after charting an assessment.
editor.outcome: Survive, die, or you decide live.
editor.outcome-notes: Your notes on how the case should end.
editor.code-branch-description: What the optional code branch is for.
editor.codes-if-not-charted-intervention: The patient codes if none of these are charted by the time below, e.g. notify-provider, rapid-response.
editor.by-sim-minute: Minutes after sim start for the code-branch check.
editor.rhythm: The monitor rhythm at the start of the sim (from data/catalogs/rhythms.json).
editor.o2: Baseline oxygen: the device (room air, nasal cannula, mask, NRB…) and, for devices with flow, liters per minute. Stored as e.g. "2 L NC".
editor.code-message: What students see when the code starts.
editor.should-recognize: Debrief-only list of what students should notice for this patient.
editor.notes-for-review: Things you still need to confirm in this case.
change.time-shift-clock: When this happens. Or tick "Instructor triggers it" to fire it yourself from Live control.
change.how-it-starts: Call light: the patient's light comes on. Staff message: a CNA/LPN/family member tells the student. Silent: only the changes below happen.
change.from: Who the staff message is from, e.g. CNA, LPN, daughter.
change.what-the-patient-says-what-is-rep: The words students get with the call light or message.
change.new-assessment-findings-one-per-l: Hidden until the student charts an assessment after this time.
setup.tags-student: If on, students see your triage tags. Usually off: prioritizing is what they are learning.
setup.tags-charge: If on, a student charge nurse sees your triage tags.
setup.reveal-manual-vitals: On: a Measure button fills in temp, RR and pain. Off: students get them from the manikin or you.
setup.pause-on-close: Pause the sim automatically if the page is closed or reloaded.
setup.delegated-assessment-reveals: If on, an assessment delegated to an LPN shows findings when they report back.
change.manual: Nothing happens at a set time; you fire it from Live control when the moment comes.
change.rhythm-monitor: Changes the rhythm on the bedside monitor at this time. With "Silent", nothing else alerts students: a monitor-only event to see who notices.
script.section: A reactive script lets this patient run itself: STATES are how the patient is (vitals, rhythm, findings), REACTIONS say what happens when the student does, or doesn't do, something. The diagram shows states as boxes and state-changing reactions as arrows; click any box or arrow to edit it. Everything you add is marked "proposed" until you approve it. Test this patient runs a dry run without touching the live sim.
script.when: What starts the reaction: a student charting an intervention (optionally with field tests such as lpm 1–4), work on an order, a MAR entry, a vital sign crossing a threshold (≤ fires on the way down, ≥ on the way up), time passing ("5 min in Hypoxic without O₂"), or another reaction or event firing (chains).
script.if: Optional extra conditions checked at the moment the trigger happens: which state the patient must (or must not) be in, actions already done or not done, vitals ranges and a sim-minute window. Leave empty to react in any state.
script.then: What happens, in order: go to a state (its vitals, rhythm and findings apply), change vitals now or as a trend, reveal new findings at the next assessment, a call light / staff message / new orders / lab result / code, or fire one of this patient's scheduled events (with its linked group).
script.repeat: Off: the reaction fires once per sim. On: it can fire again each time its trigger happens (up to "Most times it can fire", default reactionMaxFires in the settings). A reaction never fires twice at the same moment, and a runaway chain is stopped with an alert to you.
script.test: Add steps (wait N minutes, chart an intervention with its fields, give a med, mark an order done, fire an event, force a state) and Run. The table shows the patient's state, vitals, what fired and why, and the alerts. Rows in amber are "nothing was done in time" changes. Uses your unsaved edits.
script.state-name: What you (and the debrief) see for this state, e.g. "Hypoxic (SpO₂ 82%)". Students never see it.
script.state-id: Short internal name (letters, numbers, dashes). Made from the name if blank. Renaming it updates every reaction that uses it.
script.review-status: proposed = drafted, needs your review (shows a Needs review badge); partial = partly checked; approved = you have checked it.
script.trend-over-minutes: 0 applies the target vitals at once. A number moves numeric vitals and BP toward the target over that many sim minutes (one step per minute). Text values (O₂ device, pain) change at once.
script.rhythm: Monitor rhythm for this state, from the rhythms catalog. Leave as no change to keep the current rhythm.
script.findings: New assessment findings for this state, one per line. They are revealed to the student at their next assessment, like a scenario change's findings.
script.teaching-note: Optional note for the debrief when the patient reaches this state, e.g. why over-oxygenating a COPD patient matters.
script.bp: Target blood pressure, like 92/58. Blank = no change.
script.hr: Target heart rate. Blank = no change.
script.rr: Target respiratory rate. Blank = no change.
script.temp-f: Target temperature in °F. Blank = no change.
script.o: O₂ text shown on the monitor and vitals (e.g. "15 L NRB"). Blank = no change.
script.trigger: Pick what starts this reaction. The fields below change to match.
script.intervention: The intervention the student charts (from the interventions catalog). Delegated work counts when the staff member reports back.
script.field-tests-combine: All of these: every field test must hold (e.g. lpm 1–4 AND device does not contain NRB). Any one of these: one is enough (e.g. lpm ≥ 10 OR device contains NRB).
script.order: The order whose work triggers this: its own charting, a delegated report, a med given, or Mark done (the same rule as order timeliness).
script.med-order: The med order on the MAR.
script.mar-result: Which MAR entry counts: given, held or not given.
script.dose-at-least: Optional: lowest dose that counts (the first number in the med text, e.g. 0.4 in "Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL").
script.vital-sign: Which vital sign to watch. Systolic/diastolic come from the BP.
script.direction: ≤ or < fire when the value falls to or below the threshold; ≥ or > when it rises. It fires when the value crosses, not again while it stays there.
script.threshold: The number the vital sign crosses.
script.minutes: How many sim minutes after the start point the reaction fires (unless one of the listed actions happened first).
script.counting-from: When the countdown starts: entering a state, an event firing, another reaction firing, or the start of the sim. If scripting is paused and resumed, countdowns restart from the resume.
script.countdown-state: The countdown starts when the patient enters this state and stops if the patient leaves it.
script.event: One of this patient's events (scenario changes).
script.fired-by: Chain this reaction to another reaction or to one of the patient's events.
script.from-sim-minute: Only react from this sim minute (0 = start of the shift).
script.reaction-name: What you see in Live control, the diagram and the debrief, e.g. "No O₂ within 5 min: hypoxic".
script.reaction-id: Short internal name starting with r-. Made from the name if blank.
script.most-times-it-can-fire: Only for reactions that repeat. Blank uses reactionMaxFires from the scenario settings.
script.starting-state: The state the patient is in when the sim starts (usually Baseline, matching the baseline vitals).
script.reaction-template: Reusable pieces such as "O₂ response" or "Fluid bolus response" (data/catalogs/reaction-templates.json plus any you saved in this browser). Adding one copies its states and reactions into this patient; ids that are taken get a suffix.
script.for-at-least-min: How long the vital sign must stay past the threshold before this fires (e.g. SpO₂ < 80 for 5 min). If it recovers in between, the clock starts again.
script.penalty-reaches: Fires when the patient's total recovery penalty rises to this percent (e.g. 40% → charge nurse calls rapid response).
live.penalty: Recovery penalty = how much late treatment costs this patient: with 20%, a treatment that would bring SpO₂ from 70 to 99 brings it to about 93. Penalties come from reactions ("SpO₂ ≤ 82 for 5+ min"), stack up to recoveryPenaltyMaxPercent, and may wear off after treatment. Add, −10% and Clear change it now (logged); the patient's vitals follow. Deterioration from neglect is always reversible by the right treatment; only a scripted code or death is not.
script.penalty: Then → Recovery penalty: late treatment helps less. Reduce recovery by a percent of the way back (20%: 70 → 99 becomes ~93) and/or cap a vital (SpO₂ recovers no further than 94). Tick which vitals it limits (none = all). Optional: wears off over N minutes once treated, and recovery N× slower. The preview uses this reaction's trigger and the patient's states.
editor.assessments: Expected answers for assessment tools at the start of the sim (the answer key). When the sim reveals assessment findings, students see these item by item; otherwise they assess the manikin and the debrief compares. Blank items aren't scripted. Script states, scenario changes and reactions can change them later. Tools marked License check needed may only be used once their license is confirmed.
script.assessment-tool: Which tool's charted score starts this reaction.
script.score-rule: Score is at or past a number (e.g. CIWA > 15, POSS ≥ 3), or rises by at least N from the student's previous score on the same tool (e.g. NIHSS +4).
script.score: The number for the score rule (the threshold, or how much it must rise).
script.short-label: Optional short text (up to 28 characters) for this reaction's arrow on the state diagram, e.g. "no O₂ 5 min". Without it the diagram shows the trigger, cut to fit.
event.builder: Add event: pick the kind of event, then fill in only what it needs. Vitals rows: pick the vital, whether it improves, worsens or is set; From is filled with what the patient will be at that point (you can change it); To shows the patient's normal range; Over is how long the change takes (instantly, seconds, minutes, hours). The line under each row reads it back in plain English.
event.outcome: What you plan to happen. The code timer runs and you still press ROSC or No ROSC in Live control; this preselects the outcome and the rhythm the monitor shows after ROSC (blank = the scenario's roscRhythm setting).
editor.codes-if-not-charted: The code branch fires if none of these interventions has been charted by the minute below.
editor.code-rhythm: The arrest rhythm the monitor shows when the code branch fires.
live.break: Break 5 / 10 / 15 (or Break… for another length) pauses the sim for that long; Extend break +5 moves the return time later. It shows "Break — back at HH:MM" (real clock time) on every screen, including the bedside monitor. Resume (or End) ends the break; it's logged in the debrief.
live.away: A student shows Away / reconnecting when their device has stopped checking in for more than awayAfterSec (45 s) while the sim runs: closed tab, crashed tablet, lost Wi-Fi. When it checks in again, the time away is logged. (In this one-page prototype a student tab is that student's device, so a student counts as away while their tab isn't the one showing.)
live.script: Patients with a reactive script (patient editor → Script). Shows the current state, countdowns that are running ("If no O₂ by 08:05 → Hypoxic": Skip cancels one) and what the patient is listening for. Force state jumps there now (its vitals apply even if you have control of vitals). Fire now runs a reaction's effects regardless of its trigger. Disable stops one reaction; Pause scripting stops this patient reacting until you resume (countdowns restart then). Manual vitals changes still work: settings.scriptedVitalsAfterInstructor decides whether the script takes back over. Everything is logged.
chart.assessments: Scored nursing tools (GCS, NIHSS, pain, CIWA…). Pick one and answer each item; the score and what it means update as you go. Check patient shows what the patient shows for that item when your instructor turned that on; otherwise assess the manikin or ask. Some tools can be delegated. Due lists reassessments your orders require.
chart.busy: You're doing this task now. It takes this long in sim time (faster at higher sim speeds), and you can't start another task on any patient until it finishes. You can still answer call lights, silence alarms, call rapid response or a code, and notify the charge nurse. Pause task steps away from it (e.g. an emergency): you're free, and Resume carries on with the time it had left (one paused task at a time; Drop task gives it up). Interrupt task stops it: nothing is charted and it shows as interrupted in the debrief. It counts as done when it finishes.
chart.next-due: Reassessments your orders require on your group's patients, soonest first, so you can plan what to do next: overdue ones are marked ‼, ones due within 15 minutes ◷. It looks an hour ahead.
chart.news2: NEWS2 is calculated from the current vitals (RR, SpO₂, oxygen, BP, HR, temperature, alertness). You don't enter anything; Record saves it to the chart with the time.
setup.assessment-tools: Which scored nursing tools students can use in the Assessments chart tab. Public tools are ticked by default. Tools marked License check needed (Braden, Wong-Baker, CAM, POSS, Morse…) are fine to try here, but confirm their license before using them in a real course (SPEC §13). Orders that require a tool the sim doesn't offer aren't timed or flagged.
setup.reveal-assessment-findings: On: when a student picks an item and clicks Check patient, they see what the patient shows (from the patient's script). Off: they assess the manikin or ask you, and type what they find; the debrief compares it with the script.
setup.grade-assessments: On: late or missed reassessments that orders require, required assessments never done, and charted scores that differ from the patient's script show as flags (thresholds in rules.json). Off: they still appear in the debrief, without flags.
editor.patient-tags: Patient tags describe the patient for finding and randomizing: license level (LPN, RN), unit, topic, age group. They are not the red/yellow/green/black triage tag. Click a chip to add or remove it. Add tag / Add group create new ones (saved in this browser's copy of data/catalogs/patient-tags.json; export it to publish).
library.patient-tags: Filter the library by patient tags (within a group any ticked tag matches; across groups all must match, e.g. RN AND (Med-surg OR Surgical)) and search by name, room, diagnosis or tag.
setup.patient-tags: Which patients the randomizer may use. Within a tag group any ticked tag matches; across groups all must match (e.g. RN AND (Med-surg OR Surgical)). The counts show how many matching patients there are of each triage color. A group can narrow it further with its own patient tags.
setup.group-patient-tags: Optional: patient tags for this group only. A tag group you tick here replaces the sim-wide choice for that group; the rest still applies.
editor.normal-ranges: This patient's own normal range for a vital, e.g. 88–92 SpO₂ for a COPD patient. It decides what counts as recovery for penalties, the event builder's "To" hint and improve/worsen, and is shown in the debrief. Blank = the usual range from data/catalogs/vitals.json.
editor.task-times: How long a task takes for this patient when it differs from the usual (e.g. an IV start on a difficult stick). Pick the task, the time and seconds or minutes. Students are busy for this long when they chart it (Sim setup → Task timers).
setup.task-timers: Charting a task (an intervention, an assessment tool, a MAR action) keeps the student busy for its time; they can't start another task until it finishes (call lights, alarms, rapid response and notifying charge still work). Times are sim time, so they scale with speed. The usual times are in the catalogs; you can override some for this sim.
setup.task-timer-mode: Screen only: the student waits the whole task time (the time is the cost when there's no manikin). Manikin: only a short lockout, because the real task already happened on the manikin. Off: no timers.
setup.manikin-lockout-fraction-of-the-ta: In Manikin mode, the lockout is this fraction of the task time (0.25 = a quarter), but never shorter than the shortest lockout.
setup.shortest-lockout-seconds: In Manikin mode, the lockout is never shorter than this many sim seconds (stops tap-tap-tap charting).
setup.delegation-queue: When every helper of a role is busy, students can queue the task for the next free one (it starts automatically and the wait is timed). Off: they must do it themselves or wait.
setup.cna-helpers: How many nursing assistants this group can delegate to. Each does one task at a time (the task's time × the CNA speed factor in staff.json, plus walking time).
setup.lpn-helpers: How many LPNs this group can delegate to. Each does one task at a time (the task's time × the LPN speed factor in staff.json, plus walking time).
chart.staff: The helpers your group can delegate to: free, busy (with what, which patient, time left) or on break, and tasks waiting for a free helper. When you delegate, a free helper of that role takes it; if none is free you can do it yourself or queue it.
charge.staff: All delegation helpers on the unit. Move a free helper to another group, send them on break or back, or change how many a group has (+ / −). Every change is logged.
command.status: Each group card shows its delegation staff ("CNAs 2/2 busy", highlighted when a role is fully busy or tasks wait for a helper), plus On track / Falling behind / Needs attention (rule in rules.json timeliness.groupStatus), its late and very late work, overdue meds, unanswered call lights, monitor alarms and flags. Patients are listed worst first with their most overdue open item. Late/very-late thresholds are in rules.json timeliness. A card flashes for a few seconds when its status gets worse (a steady outline if reduced motion is on).
debrief.states: For patients with a reactive script: each state the patient went through, when, and why (a student action, nothing done in time, a vitals threshold, a scheduled event, another reaction, or the instructor). Red rows changed because nothing was done in time. Teaching notes come from the state (patient editor → Reactive script).
debrief.assessments: Each assessment tool the student charted, compared with what the patient's script expected at that moment: score and interpretation, the items that differed, and a red Missed high risk when a high-risk result was charted as lower risk. Below: reassessments the orders required that were late or never done. Flags come from the assessment-mismatch, assessment-overdue and required-assessment-missing rules (rules.json; off when grading is off in Sim setup).
debrief.tasks: Timed tasks (Sim setup → Task timers): when each started, how long it took, and whether it finished, was interrupted (not charted) or was ended early by you. Busy vs not-on-a-task time, and anything on this student's patients (call lights, orders, meds, reassessments, alarms) that went late while they were tied up.
debrief.delegation: Each task this student delegated: when, to which helper, how long it waited for a free helper (queued tasks are marked) and when it was done. Utilization = how much of each group's helper time was spent on tasks so far.
debrief.timeliness: Each order and scheduled med for this student's patients: when it became active or due, when it was done, minutes taken, and On time / Late / Very late / Never done (thresholds in rules.json timeliness).
live.cases: Each case template ("Cardiac 1") becomes a different patient in each sim: name, age, sex, baseline vitals and labs within their ranges, and drugs from their class. The same patient stays the same through reloads, rejoins and the debrief. Reroll (before Start) picks a new variant for one patient; Undo reroll goes back. Lock variant saves exactly this patient on the case so new sims reuse it (first use of the case). Students never see the case title.
editor.case-template: A case template is a reusable case. Each sim makes its own patient from it with a seed: a random name from the name pools (data/catalogs/names.json), an age in the age range, the sex you pick (or either), vitals and labs within their ranges, and one drug per medication class. The name, age and sex in Demographics are the case as written (the demo uses them). The case title is instructor-only.
editor.placeholders: Write texts once for every variant. {firstName} {lastName} {fullName} {age} {sex} {room}; pronouns {he/she} {He/She} {his/her} {His/Her} {him/her} {Mr/Ms}; any male/female word pair such as {wife/husband} or {Dad/Mom} (male first); this patient's baseline {bp} {hr} {rr} {spo2} {tempF}; the first lab value {lab.wbc}; the class drug {med.doac} (lowercase), {med.doac.Name} (capitalized), {med.doac.dose}, {med.doac.route}, {med.doac.freq}. Unknown placeholders are left as typed, and the variant check lists them.
editor.vital-ranges: Fixed = every variant uses the Baseline vitals value. Range = each variant picks a value in the range. The warnings below say when a range could start a variant past a threshold the case reacts to (a notify parameter, a reaction) or outside this patient's target range. Check variants runs the script on 24 variants to be sure every reaction, state and threshold still behaves as written.
editor.lab-ranges: Fixed = the value as written. Range = each variant picks a value (same decimals as the written value). Teaching point = always the written value (e.g. a lactate of 2.8 the case is built around), even if a range is set. A range that crosses the reference range makes some variants flag differently, so it warns.
editor.med-classes: Fixed = the drug as written. Any from a class = each variant picks one drug from data/catalogs/med-classes.json and uses it everywhere: home meds, the order's medication and text, the MAR, PRN and hold rules, allergy checks and timeliness. A drug the patient is allergic to is never picked, and you can exclude drugs for this case. The same drug as written keeps the written dose and frequency.
editor.case-code: A short code for this case that instructors see everywhere, e.g. "(C1) Robert Miller" in the Overview, drawers and the debrief. Suggested from the title (Cardiac 1 → C1, Heart failure 1 → HF1) and unique in the library; change it if you like. Students never see it.
